data.name: Brazil
data.summary: Brazil taxes residents on worldwide income. Since 2024 (Law 14,754/2023) income and gains from financial investments abroad are taxed annually at a flat 15%. From 2026 (Law 15,270/2025) dividends from Brazilian companies above BRL 50,000 a month per company bear 10% withholding, and a minimum tax of up to 10% applies to total income above BRL 600,000 (full 10% above BRL 1.2 million). Inheritance and gifts are taxed by the states (ITCMD, capped at 8%; Sao Paulo 4% flat in 2026). No wealth tax.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Resident individuals: 15% annual tax on foreign financial investment income and gains (Law 14,754/2023); 15%-22.5% on other capital gains; 15% on Brazilian exchange-traded equity gains; 10% WHT on large Brazilian dividends plus the IRPFM minimum tax from 2026; state ITCMD on inheritances and gifts.
regimes.eligibility: Holders of a permanent visa are resident from arrival; holders of a temporary visa without a local employment contract become resident after 183 days of presence within 12 months (PwC Residence).

capital_gains.summary: Gains on financial investments held abroad (including foreign listed shares and funds) are taxed annually at a flat 15% under Law 14,754/2023, separately from other income. Gains on shares sold on the Brazilian stock exchange are taxed at 15% (20% day trades). Other capital gains (unlisted shares, real estate in Brazil or abroad) are taxed progressively: 15% up to BRL 5 million, rising to 22.5% on the part above BRL 30 million.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Small monthly sales of Brazilian shares (up to BRL 20,000) are exempt (not re-verified). Foreign currency gains on cash held abroad follow specific rules.

capital_gains.rate_basis: PwC Other taxes: 15% flat on foreign financial investments (from 1 Jan 2024); progressive 15%-22.5% capital gains (top band above BRL 30 million) for other assets incl. assets abroad; 15% on Brazilian stock-exchange gains. Top band rates used for a large private business or real estate gain.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Day-trade gains taxed at 20%. Individuals are not generally recharacterised as traders; business activity is normally carried on through companies.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide; gains on foreign financial investments taxed on realisation once a year at 15% with no deductions.

dividends.summary: From 1 January 2026 a Brazilian company withholds 10% on the whole monthly amount when it distributes more than BRL 50,000 in a month to the same resident individual. Dividends also count towards the new minimum individual income tax (IRPFM): 0%-10% on income between BRL 600,000 and BRL 1.2 million and 10% above, with credit for tax already paid. Foreign dividends are taxed at a flat 15% annually under Law 14,754/2023.

dividends.withholding_outbound: 10% WHT on dividends to non-residents from 2026 (treaty rates cannot increase it); 15%/25% on interest and royalties.
dividends.treaty_network: About 40 treaties (incl. Argentina, Austria, Belgium, Canada, Chile, China, France, India, Italy, Japan, Luxembourg, Mexico, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Singapore, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, UAE); UK, Colombia, Paraguay pending. No US treaty (reciprocity recognised for credits).
dividends.holding_company_notes: Profits of controlled foreign entities held by individuals are taxed annually at 15% on an accrual basis (Law 14,754/2023); trusts are look-through.

wealth_tax.summary: No net wealth tax (the constitutional large-fortunes tax has never been enacted).

inheritance.summary: ITCMD is a state tax on inheritances and gifts, levied on the recipient's acquisition at up to 8% (Senate cap). EC 132/2023 makes progressive rates mandatory and LC 227/2026 (Jan 2026) set national rules, including taxation of assets abroad, but each state must legislate. Sao Paulo (scored here) still applies a single 4% rate in 2026; bills for 1%-4% or up to 8% are pending.
inheritance.regional_differences: Rates vary by state (2%-8%; Deloitte: progressive 2% up to 8%). From 2026 movable property is taxed by the state of the deceased's or donor's domicile; real estate by its location (LC 227/2026).
inheritance.important_exceptions: STF (Dec 2024): no ITCMD on VGBL/PGBL pension plan payouts at death. A transitional pending change: Sao Paulo bills PL 7/2024 (up to 8%) and PL 409/2025 (1%-4%).

income.name: Brazil

income_tax.summary: Brazilian residents pay progressive federal income tax (monthly table from January 2026: 0% to 27.5%, annualised below). From 2026 Law 15.270/2025 adds a monthly reduction that zeroes tax up to BRL 5,000 a month, phasing out at BRL 7,350, and a minimum tax on very high incomes. Employees pay progressive INSS of 7.5%-14% up to BRL 8,475.55 a month; contribuintes individuais pay 20% up to the same ceiling (11% under the simplified plan).
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Contribuinte individual: 20% of income between the minimum wage (BRL 1,621.00) and the ceiling BRL 8,475.55 a month (maximum BRL 1,695.11); the simplified plan is 11% of the minimum wage only (BRL 178.31) with reduced benefits; PwC also mentions 5%, 11% or 20% depending on conditions. Self-employed income of residents is taxed through the monthly carne-leao on the same progressive table. Employee effective rate 0.1166 = maximum monthly INSS BRL 988.09 / ceiling BRL 8,475.55, computed from the progressive table. Contribuinte individual rates (5% low-income optional/MEI, 11% simplified, 20% normal) confirmed on the INSS 2026 table page.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No municipal income tax on individuals (Sao Paulo levies ISS services tax on businesses, not modelled). Brackets are the January 2026 monthly table multiplied by 12.

open_questions: Brackets are on taxable income after INSS and the simplified deduction. Law 15.270/2025 (art. 3-A reduction, read on the Receita 2026 tables page) zeroes annual tax up to BRL 60,000 of taxable income and phases out linearly (BRL 8,429.73 - 0.095575 x income) to zero at BRL 88,200; it is not in the brackets because it affects only incomes below BRL 88,200, well under both personas (nomad USD 60k, expat USD 150k).

Minimum tax (art. 16-A of Law 15.270, read in the Planalto text 2026-10-15): from tax year 2026, individuals with total receipts above BRL 600,000 owe at least a rate on all receipts (including exempt and exclusively-taxed income) that rises linearly from 0% at BRL 600,000 to 10% at BRL 1,200,000 (rate = receipts/60,000 - 10), less ordinary IRPF, withholding and the art. 16-B reducer. It is a floor of at most 10% of receipts, below the ordinary 27.5% marginal scale on salary or professional income, so it does not change the brackets for the expat (USD 150k) or the nomad; it bites only when much of the income is exempt or taxed separately (dividends, financial income).
13th salary and dividend withholding (10% above BRL 50,000/month) not modelled.

Employee rate 0.1166 is an effective rate at the ceiling: maximum INSS BRL 988.09 (7.5/9/12/14% progressive table, Portaria MPS/MF 13 of 9 Jan 2026, read on gov.br/inss) / ceiling BRL 8,475.55; below the ceiling the effective rate is lower.

PwC (deductions page, 2026): taxpayers may instead take a standard deduction of 20% of gross taxable income capped at BRL 17,640 from January 2026, 'in lieu of the above itemised deductions' (including INSS). Above about BRL 88,200 a year it exceeds the maximum INSS (about BRL 11,860), so social_security_deductible = 1 and a bracket base 'after INSS and the simplified deduction' must not apply both; check how the model combines them.

regimes.name: Digital nomad visa (VITEM XIV)
regimes.description: Temporary residence for remote workers with no Brazilian employment relationship. Requires proof of at least USD 1,500 a month from a foreign source or USD 18,000 in bank funds, health insurance and a clean record. It does not change tax: holders without a Brazilian employment contract become tax resident after 183 days of presence within 12 months and are then taxed on worldwide income at ordinary rates.
regimes.duration_note: One year, renewable once for another year at the Federal Police (per the embassy page).

income.residence_routes: EU and US citizens can enter visa-free as tourists but cannot work; remote workers use the VITEM XIV digital nomad visa (USD 1,500 monthly foreign income or USD 18,000 funds), valid one year, renewable once. Skilled employees need a work visa tied to a Brazilian employer (temporary residence with work authorisation from the Ministry of Labour); permanent residence routes (family, investment, long residence) exist but were not researched. Nationals of Mercosur and associated states have a separate residence-agreement route.

succession.name: Brazil
succession.summary: Half of the estate is reserved to the necessary heirs (descendants, ascendants, spouse) and a will cannot touch it (Civil Code arts. 1.846, 1.845). Succession follows the law of the deceased's last domicile, and Brazilian courts alone decide on Brazilian real estate, so a foreign resident cannot opt out. Brazil has no trust law and only charitable-type foundations.
succession.reserved_share: Necessary heirs: descendants, ascendants and spouse (Código Civil art. 1.845). The legítima is one half of the estate (art. 1.846); the other half can be left freely by will.
succession.foreign_law_note: The law of the deceased's last domicile governs succession (LINDB art. 10); for property in Brazil of a foreign deceased, the foreign law applies for the benefit of the Brazilian spouse and children only if it is more favourable to them (art. 10 par. 1). Brazilian courts have exclusive jurisdiction over real estate in Brazil (CPC art. 23). No choice of law by the testator was found.
succession.trust_note: There is no general trust law. The only trust-like device is the fideicomisso, a substitution in a will (Civil Code arts. 1.951-1.960), limited to one generation. Brazil is not a party to the Hague Trusts Convention, and the treatment of foreign trusts is not settled in the sources found. Foundations (Civil Code arts. 62-69) may be created only for religious, moral, cultural or assistance purposes (art. 62 sole paragraph), so a family foundation is not possible.
open_questions: Treatment of foreign trusts by Brazilian courts and the Receita Federal (including ITCMD on trust assets) was not sourced.
Brazilian tax reform and any bill on the legítima or on trusts was not checked.

immigration.name: Brazil
immigration.summary: Brazil offers residence for a R$ 1 million property purchase (R$ 700,000 in the North and Northeast; four years, then indefinite) or R$ 500,000 (R$ 150,000 in priority sectors) into a Brazilian company. Remote workers can use a one-year digital nomad visa (USD 1,500 a month or USD 18,000 in the bank). All passports use the same routes; nationals of Portuguese-speaking countries naturalise faster.
immigration.naturalisation: Four years of residence (Lei 13.445/2017, art. 65), Portuguese communication and a clean record; one year for nationals of Portuguese-speaking countries under the Constitution; extraordinary naturalisation after 15 years.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: Brazil does not require a naturalising foreigner to renounce (general position; not source-checked in this session).

routes.name: Residence by real estate investment (RN CNIg 36/2018)
routes.summary: Four-year residence for buying at least R$ 1,000,000 of urban property (R$ 700,000 in the North and Northeast), convertible to indefinite residence.
routes.requirements: Minimum R$ 1,000,000, reducible by up to 30% for properties in the North and Northeast; several properties can be added; each co-owner must reach the minimum; financing above the minimum is allowed; funds must come from abroad. Initial authorisation 4 years, then indefinite term on showing the investment is maintained. A law-firm page (25 July 2026) cites RN 36/2018 and no successor; the Ministry of Justice and Labour norms were not read.
routes.investment_options: R$ 700,000 minimum in the North and Northeast regions.
routes.physical_presence: At least 14 days (consecutive or split) in every two-year period
routes.tax_note: Temporary residents without local employment become tax resident after 183 days in a 12-month period (PwC); a permanent visa makes tax residence from arrival.

routes.name: Digital nomad visa (VITEM XIV)
routes.summary: A one-year visa, renewable once, for remote workers earning USD 1,500 a month or holding USD 18,000. It does not convert to residence.
routes.requirements: Created by CNIg/MJSP Normative Resolution 45 of 2021 (per secondary sources): foreign-source income of USD 1,500 a month (USD 18,000 a year), or USD 18,000 in a bank balance; health insurance. One year, renewable once for a two-year maximum. Dependants file separately. Staying 183 days in 12 months can make the holder tax resident.
routes.physical_presence: Up to 1 year per grant, renewable once
routes.tax_note: Tax residence after 183 days in any 12 months (one source says 184); worldwide income then taxable.
